steps.title: Inspect the Motherboard
steps.subtitle: Complete the incoming physical inspection under ESD controls.
items: Wear the required PPE, gloves, and ESD wrist strap.
Remove the motherboard from its ESD bag and inspect it thoroughly.
Look for bent pins, damaged connectors, missing components, contamination, cracks, or other physical damage.
If damage is found, mark the location with a yellow arrow sticker and return the motherboard to ZTP.
steps.warning: Do not install or test a physically damaged motherboard.

steps.title: Verify Identity and Test History
steps.subtitle: Scan the motherboard and confirm it is eligible for testing.
items: Scan the MRS ticket into OSV Portal.
Scan or enter the motherboard serial number.
Confirm the tag serial number matches the serial number physically attached to the motherboard.
Check whether the motherboard was previously tested.
If it was previously tested, notify ZTP and do not test it again.
steps.warning: Do not continue with a mismatched serial number, incorrect MRS ticket, or duplicate test record.

steps.title: Check Tester Connections
steps.subtitle: Confirm all required tester peripherals are present and connected.
items: Keyboard for Linux input.
Mouse for script selection and log transfer.
Scanner for motherboard and ticket information.
OS USB for booting and running the approved scripts.
USB-to-RJ45 adapter for network access and ping testing.
Inspect each connection for looseness or visible damage.
steps.warning: Correct missing, loose, or damaged connections before installing the motherboard.

steps.title: Install Golden Components
steps.subtitle: Build the approved motherboard test configuration in the required order.
items: Install all approved golden DIMMs.
Install the approved golden CPU and heatsink.
Install the approved M.2 device and any other required golden components.
Place the motherboard on tester position 1, the motherboard tray, and push it into position.
Install and fully seat the FPGA and riser.
Complete tester positions 1 through 5 in the numbered order shown by the approved tester layout.
steps.warning: Do not power on the tester if any component, riser, cable, or motherboard edge is not fully seated.

steps.title: Power On and Monitor LEDs
steps.subtitle: Observe tester startup and motherboard status indicators.
items: Turn on the tester power switch.
Allow approximately 15 minutes for the motherboard to complete boot-up.
Monitor the four LEDs near the CP card area.
Confirm all four LEDs continue flashing green.
steps.warning: If the LEDs flash red or only three LEDs flash, power off the tester and wait until the Power LED is completely off before restarting.

steps.title: Run the Motherboard Test
steps.subtitle: Launch the approved Linux test selections in sequence.
items: After the operating system boots, run EC_OSV.SH from the desktop.
Select C2789_Gridcoin.
Select 7UMB_Fixture.
Start the test.
Allow the test to run until the application reports the final result.
steps.warning: Use the exact approved script and menu sequence.

steps.title: Review the Test Result
steps.subtitle: Validate a passing result or document the specific failure evidence.
items: For PASS, confirm the test logs were copied to the designated test logs folder.
For FAIL, highlight the failed test and select View Log.
Review the log and identify the actual failed test or failure message.
Record the specific failure, such as Test Inventory FW Version.
Retain the applicable logs with the MRS or local test record.
steps.warning: Do not document only the word Failed. Record the actual failed test and evidence shown in the log.

steps.title: Remove Components and Reinspect
steps.subtitle: Return the test setup and motherboard safely after testing.
items: Power down using the approved process.
Remove all golden components.
Return each golden component to its correct storage location.
Inspect the motherboard again for test-related damage.
If damage is found, notify OSV leadership, update OSV Portal, and create the required physical-damage ticket.
steps.warning: Maintain ESD controls throughout component removal and final inspection.

steps.title: Complete the Tag and Disposition
steps.subtitle: Verify identification, result information, and motherboard packaging.
items: Verify the technician Name/ID.
Verify the test date.
Verify the motherboard serial number.
Verify the ZT stock code.
Verify the detailed test result and failure description when applicable.
Place the ticket in the traveler sleeve.
Return the motherboard to the correct ESD bag.
Place it on the ESD cart for ZTP pickup.
steps.warning: Always verify that the motherboard is returned to its matching ESD bag.

steps.title: Complete Shift Records
steps.subtitle: Provide the required Test Lab Records check-in/check-out evidence.
items: Export the Test Lab Records list from MES.
Filter the list to the components tested during the shift.
Capture the filtered results using Windows+Shift+S.
Post the screenshot in the Test Lab Records Check-in/out chat.
Verify ZTP closes the records by close of business the next day.
If records remain open, request that ZTP close them.
steps.warning: Confirm every motherboard tested during the shift is included in the evidence and eventually closed.
